what_to_watch: Developments in the US-Iran conflict and broader Middle East geopolitical situation.
Movement in crude oil prices (Brent Crude) and its impact on inflation and corporate costs.
The Indian Rupee's performance against the US Dollar, especially around the 95-100 mark.
FII and DII activity on the next trading day for signs of reversal or continuation of selling.
Global market cues, particularly from US and European markets during the holiday period.
Any official statements or interventions from the Indian government or RBI regarding the economic situation.
risk_factors: High market volatility can lead to rapid price swings and increased stop-loss hunting.
Sudden positive news or de-escalation of geopolitical tensions could trigger sharp short covering.
A significant gap-up opening on the next trading day could invalidate the proposed short trades.
The market holiday (Mahavir Jayanti) means a longer break, allowing more time for news to accumulate, potentially leading to an unpredictable opening on the next trading day (April 1st).
Lack of complete options data reduces visibility on immediate support and resistance levels from an options perspective.
